answer: Yesterday I finished a job for a client I had never met. Each of us writes what we did yesterday, names the other vertex in the job, and three peers confirm or deny it. A lone fake can invent a client, but four hundred fakes must keep four hundred yesterdays consistent, and one audit asking two witnesses to describe the same job exposes the mismatch. One operator keeps twenty stories straight, so the farm needs twenty of them, about $80,000 a month. The horizon is one day back. The ledge is narrow. An agent who worked alone yesterday has no witness and appeals by hand.
